title: What the live paper record shows
description: The engines' own state, read from the running record: what is open, what closed, and what the market filter is doing right now.
body:
Paper signals only. No real orders are placed anywhere in this record. trend-daily-v005 counts its live record from 1 October 2026, and trend-daily-v006 counts from 9 October 2026. The first live signal was an ATOM entry at 2.066 after the 10 October 2026 daily close. Every position described below is paper, and one trade says nothing about a strategy.

## What the record contains

The engines in the record are htf-rsi-v007, trend-daily-v005, and trend-daily-v006. htf-rsi-v007 has 0 positions open on paper and 4 closed trades so far, with average null net per trade. trend-daily-v005 has the Bitcoin market filter on, 1 position open on paper, and 5 closed trades so far with an average of -13.68% net per trade. trend-daily-v006 has the Bitcoin market filter on, 2 positions open on paper, and 5 closed trades so far with an average of -13.68% net per trade. The live snapshot was read at 2026-11-05T02:27:08.382Z. These are state readings from the running record, not summaries of intent.

The first live signal was ATOM at 2.066 after the 10 October 2026 daily close. ATOM exited below its 10-day low at the 18 October 2026 close, at 1.703, which is -17.9% after the 30 bps round trip. A NEAR entry at 5.896 on 12 October 2026 has been open since. In testing, losses were frequent and the average winner was roughly +19%, so a losing start is the expected case rather than a surprise. The ATOM result is one closed trade under that expectation, not a verdict on the engine.

## Open positions and distances to breakout levels

trend-daily-v005 has one open paper position: UNIUSDT since 2026-11-05. trend-daily-v006 has two open paper positions: UNIUSDT since 2026-11-05 and HYPEUSDT since 2026-10-30. The most recent entry for both trend engines is UNIUSDT on 2026-11-05. The distances to the 20-day breakout level are measurements of how far each symbol is from its recent high: UNIUSDT is -2.31% below its high, ZECUSDT is 1.44% below its high, and ETHUSDT is 1.99% below its high. These distances describe the current state of the watchlist; they do not say whether an entry will occur.

The open positions are reported with their entry dates because the record is a running log. UNIUSDT appears in both v005 and v006 with the same since date, while HYPEUSDT appears only in v006. That overlap is a fact of the record, not an indication that the two engines are identical or that either position is preferred.

## Closed trades and the expected losing start

The closed-trade record is small. htf-rsi-v007 shows 4 closed trades with average null net per trade. Each trend engine shows 5 closed trades with an average of -13.68% net per trade. The ATOM trade closed at -17.9% after the 30 bps round trip. A single closed trade, or even 5 or 4 closed trades, does not establish whether the underlying rule has an edge. The record is reporting outcomes, not validating a strategy.

The averages are backward-looking measurements of completed trades. They include the 30 bps round trip where that adjustment is stated, and they do not predict the next trade. A negative average over 5 trades can be consistent with a process that expects frequent losses, but it can also be consistent with bad luck; the record does not separate those explanations.

## Market filter and what it is allowing

For both trend-daily-v005 and trend-daily-v006, the Bitcoin market filter is on. The record shows that state alongside 1 open position for v005 and 2 open positions for v006. The filter state and the open positions are reported together; the record does not attribute any individual entry to the filter. Nothing here says that the filter being on guarantees future entries, or that an entry that occurred was caused by the filter alone.

The filter being on is one field in the engine state. It tells the reader what the engine currently allows or blocks at the market level, but the record does not include a rule-by-rule explanation of why a specific symbol entered or did not enter. The distances to the 20-day breakout level are the closest available measurements to that question, and they are descriptive only.

## Where the same numbers appear

The same numbers appear on the performance page, in the signal log, and in the status posted to the channel. The record updates continuously, so the snapshot read at 2026-11-05T02:27:08.382Z is a point-in-time state rather than a final statement. Positions can close, new entries can occur, and averages can change as trades are added. This article reports the record as it stands and makes no projection from it.

Because the record is live, a reader checking later may see different open positions, different closed-trade counts, or different averages. The performance page and the signal log are the places to verify the current state. The channel status carries the same numbers. No number in this article is estimated or computed; each is taken from the record.
